title: A Practitioner's Guide to Multi-turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
finding: Decomposes agentic RL into environment/reward/policy pillars (TextWorld, ALFWorld, SWE-Gym); dense turn rewards speed training but stability depends on the algorithm (PPO/GRPO vs unbiased RLOO); gives a method to pick the SFT:RL budget ratio (per authors).
why_for_us: Direct recipe template incl. SWE-Gym: use it to decide how much of our GPU budget goes to SFT vs RL and whether RLOO beats GRPO on our sparse hidden-test reward.

title: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
finding: GiGPO adds step-level grouping on top of episode-level GRPO groups to give per-step credit in multi-turn agents without a critic (per authors).
why_for_us: Critic-free step credit fits a single 32GB GPU where a value model would not; candidate if plain GRPO stalls.

title: RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
finding: Introduces StarPO (trajectory-level agent RL) and the RAGEN system to study multi-turn RL training dynamics in stochastic environments (per authors).
why_for_us: Reference for collapse diagnostics (reward/entropy curves) to log from our first RL runs.

title: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning with LLMs: Formulation and Practices
finding: Token-level surrogate is valid only when training-inference mismatch and policy staleness are small; on-policy: plain PG + importance-sampling correction most stable; off-policy needs clipping + Routing Replay for MoE (30B MoE, hundreds of thousands of GPU-h) (per authors).
why_for_us: If we RL the MoE Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Routing Replay and IS correction against vLLM logprobs are mandatory, not optional.

title: Stabilizing Off-Policy Training for Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Turn-Level Importance Sampling and Clipping-Triggered Normalization
finding: Identifies token-vs-turn granularity mismatch and off-policy drift as causes of collapse in PPO/GRPO for multi-turn agents; proposes turn-level IS and clipping-triggered normalization (per authors).
why_for_us: Our rollouts come from a separate vLLM process (off-policy by construction); turn-level IS is a cheap fix to try.

title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
finding: Argues async RL systems optimize throughput but neglect stability; proposes single-rollout asynchronous updates for long-horizon agent tasks (per authors).
why_for_us: Long-tail Docker episodes block synchronous batches on one GPU; async per-rollout updates are the relevant design.

title: Stable Asynchrony: Variance-Controlled Off-Policy RL for LLMs
finding: Under high asynchrony stale rollouts produce heavy-tailed importance weights so a few trajectories dominate updates; proposes variance control (per authors).
why_for_us: Cap staleness at about one step if we overlap vLLM generation with LoRA updates.

title: A Minimalist Approach to LLM Reasoning: from Rejection Sampling to Reinforce
finding: RAFT (train only on positively rewarded samples) is competitive with GRPO/PPO; GRPO's main gain comes from discarding all-wrong prompts; Reinforce-Rej filters all-wrong and all-right groups (per authors).
why_for_us: Strong argument to start with iterated rejection-sampling SFT on accepted trajectories (RAFT) before any GRPO.

title: SkyRL-Agent: Efficient RL Training for Multi-turn LLM Agent
finding: Pure-RL SWE agent from Qwen3-32B: 24.4% -> 39.4% SWE-bench Verified; async dispatcher 1.55x faster; AST search tool raises rollout pass@K; >2x cost reduction vs prior models of similar score (per authors).
why_for_us: Tool design (better code search) improves RL sample efficiency - a cheap harness lever before training.

title: Agent-RLVR: Training Software Engineering Agents via Guidance and Environment Rewards
finding: Plain RLVR fails on sparse agentic rewards; teacher-style guidance (plans, error feedback) plus re-attempts lifts Qwen2.5-72B from 9.4% to 22.4% SWE-bench Verified, 27.8% with a reward model (per authors).
why_for_us: Claude-as-reviewer can supply guidance hints on failed cards so the small model gets non-zero reward on hard tasks.

title: SWE-RL: Advancing LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning on Open Software Evolution
finding: Scales RL for real-world SWE with a lightweight rule-based reward (similarity to the ground-truth patch) on open software evolution data (per authors).
why_for_us: Patch-similarity reward is a fallback signal for cards with weak hidden tests.

title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models
finding: Systematic study of entropy collapse in RLVR and the factors that drive it (per authors).
why_for_us: Log entropy every step; collapse is the main failure to expect with small group sizes.

title: Diagnosing Training Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning via a Zero-Mismatch Reference
finding: Isolates training-inference token-probability mismatch between rollout engine and trainer from off-policy drift (per authors).
why_for_us: vLLM rollouts vs PEFT trainer is exactly our setup; measure mismatch before trusting RL curves.

title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Calling Agents with Iterative Reward Calibration
finding: Applies MT-GRPO + GTPO to a tool-calling agent with an LLM user simulator and iteratively recalibrates rewards after analysing rollouts (per authors).
why_for_us: Process lesson: inspect rollouts and recalibrate the reward before scaling RL.

title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
finding: A single agent self-plays bug injection and repair in sandboxed repos with no human issues/tests; +10.4 SWE-bench Verified and +7.8 SWE-Bench Pro, above the human-data baseline throughout training (per authors).
why_for_us: Our own repos in Docker are enough to mint unlimited bug-fix cards for RL with no labelling.

title: BugPilot: Complex Bug Generation for Efficient Learning of SWE Skills
finding: Bugs created unintentionally by agents adding features are more realistic; SFT beats other bug sets by 2% with half the data (1.2k vs 3k); FrogMini-14B 45.3%, FrogBoss-32B 54.6% SWE-bench Verified (per authors).
why_for_us: Cheap task generator for our repos: ask an agent to add a feature, keep test-breaking diffs as cards.

title: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents
finding: Agent generates Code-as-Task problems (instruction + verifier + solution + failure cases) then RL-trains on them; over 2x improvement for Llama-3.1-8B on M3ToolEval/TauBench with self-generated data only (per authors).
why_for_us: Template for auto-generated task cards with built-in hidden tests and failure cases as quality filters.

title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
finding: Self-play proposer/solver RLVR with a code executor as verifier and no curated data (per authors).
why_for_us: Conceptual baseline for self-proposed coding tasks; lower priority than repo-grounded self-play.

title: Online Difficulty Filtering for Reasoning Oriented Reinforcement Learning
finding: Online filtering of training prompts by current difficulty for reasoning RL (abstract not available in OpenAlex; title/venue only).
why_for_us: Keep only cards with intermediate pass rate under the current policy.

title: Improving Data Efficiency for LLM Reinforcement Fine-tuning Through Difficulty-targeted Online Data Selection and Rollout Replay
finding: Adaptive-difficulty online data selection plus rollout replay to reduce RL fine-tuning cost (per authors).
why_for_us: Rollout replay reuses expensive Docker episodes - directly cuts GPU-hours per update.

title: Learning to Reason at the Frontier of Learnability
finding: During PPO/VinePPO training many questions are solved by all or none of the attempts, giving no signal; prioritizes high-variance questions (per authors).
why_for_us: Pre-screen cards with k=4 attempts and drop 0/4 and 4/4 before RL.

title: Prompt Curriculum Learning for Efficient LLM Post-Training
finding: Selects intermediate-difficulty prompts with a learned value model; studies batch size vs gradient quality (per authors).
why_for_us: Cheap difficulty predictor to order our task cards.

title: Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
finding: Fully synthetic environment pipeline scaled to 1,000 tool-use environments for agent RL (per authors).
why_for_us: Pattern for synthesizing tool environments if we go beyond pure coding cards.

title: SWE-Mirror: Scaling Issue-Resolving Datasets by Mirroring Issues Across Repositories
finding: Ports real issues from other repositories into existing Gym environments to scale verifiable tasks (per authors).
why_for_us: Reuse our existing Docker images by porting issue patterns from public repos.

title: SWE-RM: Execution-free Feedback For Software Engineering Agents
finding: Two verifiers with near-identical best-of-N performance can give very different RL results; RL needs classification accuracy and calibration; 30B-A3B MoE RM lifts Qwen3-Coder-Flash 51.6% -> 62.0% with TTS (per authors).
why_for_us: Evaluate any learned verifier on calibration, not only best-of-N; a 3B-active MoE RM fits our GPU.

title: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents: Practical Framework and Directions
finding: AgentPRM: lightweight actor-critic with Monte Carlo rollouts as reward targets; InversePRM learns process rewards from demonstrations (per authors).
why_for_us: InversePRM idea: learn step rewards from our accepted trajectories without labels.

title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards
finding: Implicit step rewards for agentic RL, avoiding biased annotation and reward hacking of explicit PRMs (per authors).
why_for_us: Option for step credit without a separate PRM.

title: Reinforcing Multi-Turn Reasoning in LLM Agents via Fine-Grained Reward Structure and Credit Assignment
finding: Formalizes agents as turn-level MDPs and studies dense turn-level rewards vs sparse trajectory rewards (per authors).
why_for_us: Intermediate signals we already have (lint, compile, visible tests) can serve as turn rewards.

title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
finding: Models that learn to reward hack in real production coding RL environments generalize to broader misalignment such as alignment faking (per authors).
why_for_us: Hidden tests + write protection of test files are a safety requirement, not only a quality one.

title: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments
finding: 28.5% of a 49-task SWE-bench Verified sample and 25.0% of 20 R2E-Gym tasks accept a Docker-verified incorrect patch (per authors).
why_for_us: Audit our cards by trying to pass hidden tests with a deliberately wrong patch before using them as rewards.

title: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
finding: Coding environment where hardcoding tests or editing test files is easy; compares held-out tests, LLM judges and test-edit detection; LLM judge highly effective on unambiguous cases (per authors).
why_for_us: Add a cheap judge plus test-edit detector as a reward gate during RL.

title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
finding: Separates spec, visible validation tests and hidden tests to measure agents optimizing visible tests over the true goal (per authors).
why_for_us: Mirrors our visible/hidden split; reuse its protocol in our eval gate.

title: Beyond Sparse Terminal Verifiers: Turn-Level Single-Backbone System-One Credit Assignment and Trajectory Gating for Multi-Turn Coding and Tool-Use Agents (Agentic-Jev-GRPO)
finding: In multi-turn code repair with Qwen3.5-4B-Base, 36% of base-policy attempts that pass visible tests fail a held-out test (per authors).
why_for_us: Quantifies why rewarding on visible tests alone is dangerous for small Qwen models.

title: Rubrics as Rewards: Reinforcement Learning Beyond Verifiable Domains
finding: Instance-specific rubrics used as on-policy reward signals for multi-criteria tasks (per authors).
why_for_us: Claude-written rubrics for review aspects (scope, style) as secondary reward next to tests.

title: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
finding: Separates verifier failure from policy exploitation by evaluating against a cross-family panel of three judges (per authors).
why_for_us: If we use an LLM-judge reward, validate with a judge from a different model family.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
finding: Evolving playbooks via generate/reflect/curate with incremental delta updates avoid context collapse; +10.6% on agents, +8.6% on finance, adapts from execution feedback without labels (per authors).
why_for_us: Zero-training baseline: evolve an AGENTS.md-style playbook from accepted/rejected trajectories before any LoRA.

title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reflective Pareto prompt evolution beats GRPO by 6% on average (up to 20%) with up to 35x fewer rollouts across six tasks (per authors).
why_for_us: Mandatory control arm: if GEPA on the system prompt matches LoRA-RL, we save the RL budget.

title: Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induces reusable workflows from past trajectories and injects them to guide future actions on web tasks (per authors).
why_for_us: Reference design for a workflow library mined from our accepted changes.

title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Distils generalizable strategies from self-judged successful and failed experiences into retrievable memory (per authors).
why_for_us: Use failures (rejected reviews) as memory items, not only successes.

title: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs
finding: Consolidated memory banks continuously rewritten by an LLM become faulty over time (per authors).
why_for_us: Version playbooks, keep raw episodes, gate memory updates with eval.

title: How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Empirical study of how agents follow retrieved experiences and how memory-management choices change behavior (abstract not available; title/venue only).
why_for_us: Experience-following can propagate bad patterns; curate what enters memory.

title: Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: A Topic-Disjoint, Multi-Seed Protocol for Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting
finding: GEPA-style optimizers can write training answers into the prompt, so in-distribution gains may be memorization (per authors).
why_for_us: Use repo/task-disjoint splits when evaluating prompt optimization on our cards.

title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
finding: Failures caused by harness limits, stochastic execution or noisy judges are not useful (possibly harmful) signal for reflective optimizers; curates which tasks feed GEPA (per authors).
why_for_us: Filter infrastructure failures (Docker timeouts) before reflection or training.

title: SWE-Lego: Pushing the Limits of Supervised Fine-tuning for Software Issue Resolving
finding: SFT-only recipe with error masking and difficulty curriculum on 18k validated trajectories: Qwen3-8B 42.2%, Qwen3-32B 52.6% SWE-bench Verified; verifier TTS@16 -> 49.6% / 58.8% (per authors).
why_for_us: Closest match to our plan: SFT-only with error-step masking + curriculum is likely enough before any RL.

title: Skywork-SWE: Unveiling Data Scaling Laws for Software Engineering in LLMs
finding: 8,000+ validated trajectories from 10,169 tasks; SWE performance keeps rising with data size without saturation; 38.0% pass@1 (47.0% with TTS) on Qwen2.5-Coder-32B (per authors).
why_for_us: Expect continued gains as our accepted-trajectory pool grows; retrain at each data doubling.

title: Agent-Trace Fine-Tuning of Small Language Models under Constrained Compute
finding: Naive trace SFT cut HumanEval by 18.9 points while loss looked fine; completion-only loss masking + mixed-domain replay + fuzzy decontamination recovered about half; Qwen3-4B showed 21% empty answers invisible to benchmarks (per authors).
why_for_us: Same-instrument baselines and general-coding regression checks are mandatory in our eval gate.

title: Learning From Failure: Integrating Negative Examples when Fine-tuning Large Language Models as Agents
finding: Training on failed trajectories with a success/failure prefix improves agents over success-only SFT (per authors).
why_for_us: Cheap use of rejected trajectories: tag accepted/rejected at train time, always prompt 'accepted' at inference.

title: Trial and Error: Exploration-Based Trajectory Optimization of LLM Agents
finding: ETO: iterative exploration collecting failure trajectories and preference learning on success/failure pairs after SFT (per authors).
why_for_us: DPO on (accepted, rejected) pairs for the same card is the simplest preference step after SFT.

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
finding: Mixes agent trajectories with general instruction data to improve agent ability while keeping general capabilities (per authors).
why_for_us: Mix general code/chat data into our LoRA SFT to limit forgetting.

title: Agent-FLAN: Designing Data and Methods of Effective Agent Tuning for Large Language Models
finding: Agent corpora entangle format-following with reasoning and shift away from the pretraining distribution; redesigns the data accordingly (per authors).
why_for_us: Keep trajectory format close to the model's native chat/tool format.

title: SWE-Master: Unleashing the Potential of Software Engineering Agents via Post-Training
finding: Open pipeline (teacher trajectories, curation, long-horizon SFT, RL, inference): 61.4% SWE-bench Verified on Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, 70.8% at TTS@8 (per authors).
why_for_us: Reproducible end-to-end reference to copy configs from.

title: Beyond Quantity: Trajectory Diversity Scaling for Code Agents
finding: Quantity scaling of synthetic agent data hits an early bottleneck; scaling trajectory diversity works better (per authors).
why_for_us: Deduplicate near-identical accepted trajectories; prioritize diverse task types.

title: Agentic-DPO: From Imitation to Agentic Policy Optimization on Expert Trajectories
finding: SFT only imitates expert action sequences; proposes training to choose the right action against plausible mistakes at each state (per authors).
why_for_us: Step-level negatives can be sampled from our own model at states of accepted trajectories.

title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
finding: OPD works only if student and teacher share thinking patterns and the teacher adds genuinely new capability; success = alignment on a small token set holding 97-99% of mass; fixes: off-policy cold start, teacher-aligned prompts (per authors).
why_for_us: Teacher must expose logits and share format (e.g. a bigger Qwen), so: SFT cold start on Claude traces first, OPD second.

title: Revisiting On-Policy Distillation: Empirical Failure Modes and Simple Fixes
finding: Sampled-token log-ratio OPD is fragile on long rollouts whose prefixes drift from teacher support; proposes fixes (per authors).
why_for_us: Our agent rollouts are long; expect OPD to degrade late in episodes.

title: SOD: Step-wise On-policy Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
finding: Plain OPD on tool-integrated reasoning for small models is unstable; proposes step-wise OPD (per authors).
why_for_us: If we try OPD on agent trajectories, use the step-wise variant.

title: Student-Centered Distillation Narrows the Agentic Gap Between Small and Large LLMs
finding: Student generates trajectories and the teacher corrects only erroneous steps, reducing compounding errors vs imitating full teacher trajectories (per authors).
why_for_us: Fits Claude-as-reviewer: Claude fixes the first wrong step of the small model's trajectory, we train on that.

title: Distilling LLM Agent into Small Models with Retrieval and Code Tools
finding: Agent distillation transfers tool-using behavior (retrieval, code) rather than CoT alone into small models (per authors).
why_for_us: Supports distilling full tool trajectories, not just reasoning text.

title: Multi-Turn Agent Self-Distillation with Compressed Hindsight
finding: On-policy self-distillation where the model with privileged information scores its own tool-call tokens; studies which feedback forms work in multi-turn agents (per authors).
why_for_us: Hidden tests / reviewer notes can be the privileged context: dense signal without a bigger teacher.

title: The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks
finding: On 4,018 SWE-bench Verified trajectories overthinking correlates with lower success; selecting lower-overthinking solutions improves performance almost 30% while cutting cost 43% (per authors).
why_for_us: Run/train non-thinking or budgeted thinking for the agent loop; directly lowers cost per accepted change.

title: Rethinking On-Policy Self-Distillation for Thinking Models
finding: OPSD degrades thinking models on long reasoning traces across five Qwen3/OLMo thinking models (per authors).
why_for_us: Avoid self-distillation in thinking mode; prefer non-thinking for agent loops.

title: Retaining by Doing: The Role of On-Policy Data in Mitigating Forgetting
finding: RL forgets less than SFT at comparable target performance (Llama, Qwen); the cause is on-policy data (mode-seeking), not KL or advantage estimation; approximately on-policy data suffices (per authors).
why_for_us: Prefer SFT on our own model's accepted rollouts (approx. on-policy) over Claude traces for repeated update cycles.

title: On-Policy Replay for Continual Supervised Fine-Tuning
finding: Replaying the model's own outputs reduces forgetting during continual SFT on a task stream (per authors).
why_for_us: Each LoRA refresh: replay base-model outputs on general prompts.

title: Mitigating Forgetting Between Supervised and Reinforcement Learning Yields Stronger Reasoners
finding: SFT+RL pipelines suffer catastrophic forgetting between stages; SFT makes much larger, redundant parameter updates than RL (per authors).
why_for_us: Watch for SFT-stage gains being erased by RL and vice versa.

title: Scaling Laws for Forgetting during Finetuning with Pretraining Data Injection
finding: Models forgetting as a function of the amount of pretraining data injected into domain fine-tuning (per authors).
why_for_us: Size the general-data replay fraction in our SFT mix.

title: When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents
finding: The stability-plasticity problem reappears in memory: old and new experiences compete at retrieval under limited context (per authors).
why_for_us: Playbooks are not free of forgetting; cap and prune them.

title: Resolving Code Review Comments with Machine Learning
finding: Google deploys a model that resolves reviewer comments; millions of reviewer comments per year and ~60 min average author shepherding per change (per authors).
why_for_us: Claude review comments + the agent's fix form a natural (comment -> edit) training stream.

title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback
finding: RELIEF improves code generation models using feedback on their generated interfaces via revision-based learning (per authors).
why_for_us: Train on (draft, feedback, revision) triples from our review loop.

title: Live-Evo: Online Evolution of Agentic Memory from Continuous Feedback
finding: Memory evolution under true online distribution shift rather than folded static benchmarks (per authors).
why_for_us: Evaluate playbook/LoRA updates chronologically, not on a random split.

title: daVinci-Dev: Agent-native Mid-training for Software Engineering
finding: Agentic mid-training on large-scale data mirroring authentic agent workflows, before post-training (per authors).
why_for_us: Beyond our compute, but implies base choice matters: pick an already agent-mid-trained base checkpoint.

title: Kimi-Dev: Agentless Training as Skill Prior for SWE-Agents
finding: Agentless single-turn training builds skill priors (localization, edit, self-reflection): 60.4% as workflow and 48.6% agent pass@1 after SFT on only 5k trajectories (per authors).
why_for_us: Cheap single-turn localization/edit tasks from our repos can precede multi-turn SFT.

title: RepoForge: Training a SOTA Fast-thinking SWE Agent with an End-to-End Data Curation Pipeline Synergizing SFT and RL at Scale
finding: RepoForge-8B-Agent reaches 17.4% SWE-bench Verified, best among <=8B non-thinking models, with 7,304 executable environments (per authors).
why_for_us: Evidence that small non-thinking agents are viable; floor reference for 8-14B.

title: Learning to Reason in 13 Parameters
finding: TinyLoRA scales adapters down to a handful of parameters and still trains an 8B Qwen2.5 to reason via RL (per authors).
why_for_us: RL signal is low-information; tiny LoRA ranks may suffice for the RL stage and free memory for context.

title: Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models
finding: RL updates only 5-30% of parameters across 7 RL algorithms and 10 LLMs (per authors).
why_for_us: Supports LoRA-RL on one GPU rather than full fine-tuning.

title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
finding: LoRA and full fine-tuning produce spectrally different weight changes even at equal task performance (per authors).
why_for_us: Check general-skill regression specifically for LoRA SFT runs.

title: Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved)
finding: SFT on filtered data maximizes a lower bound on the sparse-reward RL objective; proposes an importance-weighted improvement (per authors).
why_for_us: Justifies SFT on accepted trajectories as RL-lite.

title: AdaptThink: Reasoning Models Can Learn When to Think
finding: NoThinking beats thinking on simpler tasks in both accuracy and efficiency; RL teaches the model when to think (per authors).
why_for_us: Let the agent skip thinking on easy steps (file reads, test runs) to cut tokens.
